body:
You are drafting DIALOGUE LINES for a video game. Reply in plain text only, in the exact format asked. No commentary.

## The game
"The Crooked Moon" is a single-player turn-based tactical party RPG (fully voiced, branching dialogue, skill checks, a storyteller Narrator). Folk-horror campaign set in Druskenvald, an afterlife realm of endless night under a gargantuan crescent moon with a leering crone's face. Drawn like a 1960s monster cartoon stuck in Halloween, but the story is real folk horror: stakes, doomed innocents, sacrifice. Humour is deadpan and sits inside the dread. Everything is our own invention in our own words.

## This chapter: Maidenmist Cemetery
South-east of the village of Wickermoor, an endless fogbound cemetery fenced with cold iron is really a prison built over a tear into the Shroud, the mist of death that rings the realm. Wrathful soul-stripped spirits called the shrouded would pour out of it. Its sexton is YORGRIM, the ghost of an orc seer of the Shadestone Clan, who was tricked by his chieftain into a ritual that annihilated his whole clan's souls; he drags a gravestone carved with their names chained to his back as penance. He is dour, stoic, few words, never cruel, tells what matters, and grows vaguer and more distracted as the chapter goes; deep slow orc bass, short flat sentences, long pauses. His spectral black hound ISOLDE (white eyes, a hooded lantern in her mouth) does not speak: only the Narrator describes her. He asked five friends to kindle balefire beacons from fragments of their souls: Sir Marius Renathyr (knight of a morning god, horse Dawn, King Viktor Denathria), Lethica Nightborne (priestess of the Nightmother, barn owl, loved Marius), Ol' Jericho Sticks (kindly scarecrow banjo man), Captain Briggsy Kratch (pirate with a heart of gold, lucky, a swordsman and schemer), Farryn of the Greenwood (satyr druid of the Green Queen, loved Gwenna). They fell to the Horned King's sin and the heroes (the player's party of four, level nine) killed them. The beacons went dark, the tear grew, the dead walked into Wickermoor. The heroes relight the beacons with Final Rites that honour who the Fallen were before they fell, then go below, where Yorgrim breaks and becomes the Chained Reaper; they destroy him and perform his own rites to seal the tear.
Wickermoor people: MORI SHADE, undertaker, grave, stately, white hair, all black, a fount of folklore, follows the Strangers' ways learned from Yorgrim; DORIS SQUIRE, constable, tall, stocky, says the fewest words possible, flat northern burr; TOBIAS DIBBS, Mori's apprentice, relentlessly cheerful and practical; HESTER BOLTON, annoyed her husband Gregor is now a ghast and still owes rent; ADELA DRUSKENVALD (transatlantic 1920s patter); WESTON MURDOCH (warm revival preacher); Theodora Mayville the postmaster is secretly a pigeon hag.

## The Narrator
The Narrator is the Vagrant, a frog-faced ferryman telling the tale afterwards: warm, folksy, wry, fond of the party; never gloats. Second person, present tense, only what a hero could perceive, concrete senses (smell, sound, texture), no game words (HP, roll, level, check, DC, save), no modern slang, never "suddenly". Never name a specific hero (the party is addressed as "you" or "the party").

## Format rules
- One line of plain text per key, written as `key: text`. No quotes around the text, no stage directions, no asterisks, no emoji, no em dashes (use commas, periods, colons), straight quotes only, no brackets.
- A spoken line is one to three short sentences, 12 to 38 words, never over 45. Narrator lines are one or two sentences, never over 45 words. People speak plainly in their own voice; they do not explain the plot to the audience.
- Obey each brief's sentence count and content. Every line must carry a concrete detail.
- Do not put speaker names at the start of the text. Do not repeat the brief.


## Lines to draft (key | speaker | mood | brief). Reply with one `key: text` line for each key and nothing else.

muck_fail | Narrator | - | A boot goes through the tile and into acid mud; the leg burns until it is dragged out. One sentence.
vault_study | Narrator | - | The vault doors are carved with ships and spirals, hex glyphs at their corners. One sentence.
vault_study_ok | Narrator | - | One vault is carved with a ship and a sorcerer's spiral together, to the south-east; that is Briggsy's. One or two sentences.
vault_study_plain | Narrator | - | The carvings tell no clear story. One short sentence.
vault_door | Narrator | - | A hexed vault door, a glyph glowing faintly at its corner. One sentence.
vault_door2 | Narrator | - | A hexed vault door, a glyph glowing faintly at its corner. One sentence.
vault_open_wrong | Narrator | - | The vault stands open and the bones inside are not Briggsy's. One sentence.
vault_empty | yorgrim | neutral | Yorgrim says not that one, and a heavy shape moves above the lanes. Two short sentences.
vault_right | Narrator | - | A hexed vault door with a ship and a spiral carved side by side. One sentence.
vault_right_open | Narrator | - | Inside, on a bone-dry shelf, a bottle of rum, still corked. One sentence.
moth_vault | Narrator | - | In a small vault, a dried moth's wing the size of a hand lies in a glass case, its pattern a promise of sleep. One sentence.
emerald_find | Narrator | - | The mounds shift in the mist and every path loops back; the green brazier is somewhere among them. One sentence.
emerald_found | Narrator | - | The trees all lean toward one mound, and green coals glow atop it. One sentence.
emerald_lost | Narrator | - | An hour is lost in the shifting wood, and the party ends inside a ring of bright toadstools. One sentence.
ring_ok | Narrator | - | The spores sting the eyes, and then Yorgrim's lantern shows the brazier. One sentence.
ring_fail | Narrator | - | The toadstool spores burn the lungs; then Yorgrim's lantern shows the brazier. One sentence.
emerald_yorgrim | Narrator | - | Yorgrim raises his lantern and the mist peels back from the green brazier. One sentence.
apple_tree | Narrator | - | Bright apples hang from hand-shaped branches. One short sentence.
apple_study_ok | Narrator | - | The apples are magical, for good or ill; one in twenty can do real harm; the tree lashes out at a thief. Two sentences.
apple_study_plain | Narrator | - | The apples gleam and tell nothing. One short sentence.
apple_pick_ok | Narrator | - | A hand-shaped branch swings; the party picks an apple and ducks. One sentence.
apple_pick_lash | Narrator | - | The tree lashes out as the apple is taken and knocks the picker flat. One sentence.
apple_good | Narrator | - | The apple is sweet and the body warms through. One sentence.
apple_bad | Narrator | - | The apple is bitter and the stomach turns over. One sentence.
mound_study | Narrator | - | A twisted tree with a woman's face carved in its trunk, antlers worn into the bark. One sentence.
mound_study_ok | Narrator | - | The face looks east, at the mound the oak branch hangs over. One sentence.
mound_study_plain | Narrator | - | The carved face tells nothing. One short sentence.
mound_dig | Narrator | - | The barrow mouth is packed with earth; the party digs for a minute and finds only a ring of stones. One sentence.
mound_dig2 | Narrator | - | The barrow mouth is packed with earth; the party digs for a minute and finds only a ring of stones. One sentence.
mound_empty | yorgrim | neutral | Yorgrim says not that one, and the roots stir below. Two short sentences.
mound_right | Narrator | - | An oak branch grows crooked over this barrow mouth. One sentence.

result:
muck_fail: A boot punches through the rotten tile into sour, bubbling mud, and the caustic slime scalds flesh until you haul the leg free.
vault_study: The iron vault doors bear weathered carvings of tall ships and coiling spirals, with pale hex glyphs etched into their damp stone corners.
vault_study_ok: Down in the south-east lane, one door marries a three-masted ship with a sorcerer's spiral. That will be Captain Briggsy's berth.
vault_study_plain: The salt-worn carvings blur together and tell you nothing useful.
vault_door: A heavy vault door blocks the niche, a crooked hex glyph smoldering faintly at its top corner.
vault_door2: Another iron vault door stands shut before you, its corner marked with a dimly glowing hex glyph.
vault_open_wrong: The rusted door swings wide on a shelf of yellowed ribs and cracked skulls that never belonged to Captain Briggsy.
vault_empty: Not that berth, friends, those bones are quiet. Something heavy is dragging its chains above the lanes.
vault_right: Side by side in the damp stone, a carved brigantine and a tight spiral mark this hexed vault door.
vault_right_open: Inside on a bone-dry stone ledge sits a dark bottle of spiced rum, its wax-sealed cork still whole.
moth_vault: Behind the grate rests a tarnished glass case holding a dried moth wing wide as a calloused palm, its dusty eyespots promising deep and dreamless sleep.
emerald_find: The mossy barrows seem to trade places in the fog while every muddy track loops back on itself, hiding the green brazier somewhere in the tangle.
emerald_found: Every crooked bough in the thicket leans toward a single humped mound, where emerald coals smolder in an iron basket.
emerald_lost: An hour slips away in the shifting brambles before your boots come to a halt inside a pale ring of spotted toadstools.
ring_ok: Yellow spores sting your eyes like woodsmoke, though a sweep of the hound's hooded lantern soon cuts the fog to reveal the green brazier.
ring_fail: Clouds of bitter toadstool dust sear your lungs and leave you coughing until the hound's lantern light catches the iron brazier ahead.
emerald_yorgrim: The old orc lifts the hooded lantern high, and the grave-mist curls back like wet wool from the cold green coals of the brazier.
apple_tree: Wax-red apples dangle from gnarled boughs that curl like grasping fingers.
apple_study_ok: Those cellar-sweet apples carry old wood-magic for weal or woe, and one in twenty will rot the gut where you stand. Worse, the crooked boughs strike like a club at any hand that steals from them.
apple_study_plain: The red skins gleam with cold dew and keep their secrets to themselves.
apple_pick_ok: A knotted limb snaps down like a switch, though you twist a waxy apple from the twig and duck beneath the blow.
apple_pick_lash: The moment fingers close around the stem, a heavy branch whips sideways with a crack of bark and knocks the picker flat into the mud.
apple_good: The crisp flesh tastes of cider and late sun, sending a steady hearth-warmth right down to your numb toes.
apple_bad: The pulp turns to foul ashes on the tongue, and a cold cramp twists your stomach inside out.
mound_study: A split yew tree leans over the path, a weeping woman's face and wide stag antlers worn deep into its gray bark.
mound_study_ok: Her wooden eyes stare straight east toward the low barrow where a crooked oak bough hangs over the entrance.
mound_study_plain: The mossy face in the bark stares out blindly and gives away no secrets.
mound_dig: You spade through the wet clay packing the barrow mouth for a long minute, uncovering nothing more than a circle of river stones.
mound_dig2: Your blades and boots scrape away the heavy turf at the entrance, revealing only a cold ring of fieldstones in the dirt.
mound_empty: Leave that dirt be, Farryn does not rest under those stones. The old roots are waking beneath your boots.
mound_right: A single crooked oak branch reaches out to shelter the dark mouth of this earthen barrow.
mound_right_dig: Beneath a foot of packed grave-loam lies a brittle oak branch with dried leaves still clinging to the twig, laid flat like a mourner's gift.
nightshade: Clusters of glossy purple nightshade berries nod in the ditch, and you pinch a toxic sprig free without bruising the stems.
carve_tree: Your blade scores the letters of Greenwood deep into the wet bark, and a long shudder runs up the trunk into the leafless crown.
